concerns.text: T031/T031b mandate 'Human pilot data (≥50 participants)' as a hard blocker with 'No synthetic fallback'. This contradicts the Plan's 'Human Data Collection Timeline' which explicitly permits 'Use synthetic calibration with explicit limitation' if human data fails. The task silently enforces a constraint (FR-010 strictness) that the Plan has already relaxed, creating a semantic conflict where the task blocks a path the Plan authorizes.

T012c/T012b implement logic to 'fail loudly' if Khan Academy source is missing. However, the Plan's 'Scope Note' explicitly reduces FR-001 scope to 'ASSISTments dataset only' because Khan Academy has 'no verified source'. These tasks build error handling for a requirement the Plan has already deleted, creating orphan work that violates the 'no silent constitution drift' principle by maintaining a dependency on a dropped scope.

T041 (computational irreducibility test) and T042 (symbolic concrete object mapper) are marked `[X]` (completed) in the task list, yet the 'Notes' section explicitly states these tasks were 'rejected' and 'to be redone' due to unverifiable nature. Marking them as complete while simultaneously flagging them as rejected creates a direct semantic contradiction, violating the requirement that task status must accurately reflect deliverable readiness.

T043-T046 are marked `[X]` (completed) in the list, but the 'Notes' section states these tasks have 'missing artifacts' (no logs, no docs, no reports) and were flagged as 'Required change'. Retaining them as completed falsely signals that FR-008 (resource limits) and SC-006 (CI monitoring) are satisfied, violating the constraint that task completion must imply deliverable verification.

T023 and T037b both implement logic to validate the 'no consecutive empty bins > 5s' distribution constraint (SC-005). This duplication of effort creates a semantic drift where the verification logic is split across two tasks, risking inconsistent implementation of the same acceptance criterion. The spec requires a single validation outcome; splitting it introduces a risk of partial compliance.
